chunks: From him, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked (and I was present) about a woman who breast-fed a boy who was her slave from her milk until she weaned him: Is it permissible for her to sell him? He said: No, he is her son from breast-feeding. It is prohibited for her to sell him and to consume his price.
He said, then he said: Did not the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'That which is prohibited due to lineage is also prohibited due to breast-feeding.'
ai.seo_question: Does breast-feeding a slave child establish a kinship bond that prevents the owner from selling them?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that breast-feeding a slave girl creates a permanent kinship bond (radāʿ) that prohibits her from selling him, as he becomes her 'son' through this act. This ruling is grounded in the Prophetic tradition that the prohibitions of breast-feeding mirror those of lineage (nasab). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the legal weight of radāʿ in determining mahram relationships and inheritance rights, extending beyond mere biological ties to include social and spiritual kinship.
